value.title: A collection of nouns and verbs for finding edge and corner cases on purpose
value.lets_workers: Plan which edges apply to a target and write every expected result before anything runs; generate labelled, seeded cases for text, numbers, dates, lists and request bodies with tested code; run them on a local build, put pages into edge states, check a video's edges and try an API's edges; store every input escaped with its digest; and turn every failure into a finding whose case becomes its regression test.

For the generated kinds, with the plan's seed and limits.
Generated text, number, date and list cases through the target's input paths.
Pages in each interface state the plan names.
Bodies, replays, leases and auth against the local build.
A different worker reruns the case on the fixed build.
The failing case is kept as a test that fails without the fix.

complements: Interface states use the screenshot design review pack's capture matrix and the accessibility audit pack's layout rules; this pack adds the states those packs do not set up, such as offline, slow network and no JavaScript.
Video edges are measured with the video QA pack's rules; this pack names the edges a whole-file check can miss, such as the poster, the loop seam and captions at cuts.
Findings, fixes, independent verification and regression guards come from the findings to fixes pack; a guard is proven by the checks of checks pack's trust rule.
Exploratory sessions find edges no catalog lists; their bugs come back here as new classes.

value.title: How edge and corner cases are planned, generated, run and recorded
value.category_reason: A reusable procedure with guardrails, followed by every verb in this pack.
lifecycle: plan-edges chooses the classes that apply to the target and writes every class's expected result before anything runs.
generate-cases runs the seeded generator with the plan's seed and limits and pins the case set by digest.
run-input-cases, check-interface-edges, check-video-edges and check-api-edges run the cases on a local build or a test page and record what happened.
record-edge-findings turns each failure into a finding whose reproduction is the case itself.
Findings go through the findings to fixes pack: reproduce, propose-fix, fix, verify-fix by a different worker, and add-regression-guard with the failing case kept as the test.
rules: Expectations come first. A result is a verdict only against an expectation pinned before the run.
One seed per plan, recorded with the generator's code digest, so anyone can regenerate the exact cases.
A 500, a crash, a hang, silent truncation, a changed meaning or half a write is always a failure, whatever the plan said.
Coverage is what ran: a class that did not run is listed as not run with its reason, never as passing.
Store inputs escaped and pinned by SHA-256; never paste a raw invisible or direction-changing character into a record.
Workers create nouns and propose verbs; they never enqueue.
techniques: Boundary values: the limit, one inside and one past it, on both sides.
Equivalence classes: one case per class of input the target should treat the same way.
Pairs: when two settings interact, such as right-to-left text at 320 pixels, run the pair as its own case.
Seeded variation: a few random cases per kind, reproducible from the seed, to reach what the catalog did not list.
sources: Boundary value analysis and equivalence partitioning are long-standing test design techniques.
Unicode, date, JSON and HTTP behavior follows the dated public sources in this pack's sources noun.
The catalogs, labels, rules and examples are written for this pack.

value.title: Input edges: the classes to try and what to ask of each
value.category_reason: A catalog of test input classes, each with the question a run answers.

classes.try: The minimum, the maximum and one past each; zero; one; exactly the length or page limit and one more.
classes.ask: Is the limit enforced where the data enters, with a message that names it?

classes.try: Nothing, one space, only spaces, a no-break space, an empty list, a null item.
classes.ask: Is empty handled once, as missing or as a value, and the same way everywhere?

classes.try: Sixty-four times the length limit, a hundred pages of items, a body past the size limit, nesting deeper than any real request.
classes.ask: Is it refused early, before it is parsed, logged or stored, with memory staying bounded?

classes.try: Combining marks, right-to-left text, direction overrides, emoji sequences, zero-width characters, lookalikes, full-width forms and case mappings that change length.
classes.ask: Does it round-trip, compare after normalizing, count as people see it and display in the right order?

classes.try: Thousands and decimal marks of other locales, other scripts' digits, a minus sign that is not a hyphen, scientific and hexadecimal forms, NaN and Infinity, integers past 2**53.
classes.ask: Is every form parsed by a stated rule and shown back, or refused with a message; never read as a different number?

classes.try: Local times that never happen and times that happen twice, half-hour and quarter-hour offsets, +14:00 and -11:00, times with no offset.
classes.ask: Is a missing or repeated local time refused or settled by a stated rule, and is every stored time unambiguous?

classes.try: The 29th of February in leap and common years, the 31st of a 30-day month, adding a month to the 31st of January, ISO week 53, leap seconds, epoch edges and far years.
classes.ask: Are impossible dates refused rather than rolled over, and are date sums stated?

classes.try: The same value twice, and values that differ only in case, spacing or normalization; two records with one id.
classes.ask: Are duplicates folded together, refused or reported by a stated rule, never silently counted twice or overwritten?

classes.try: Already sorted, reversed, equal sort keys, numbers written as text, capitals and accents.
classes.ask: Is the order the one people expect, stable for equal keys, by the reader's language rules?

classes.try: The same action twice in quick succession, two tabs editing one record, two workers claiming one item, a read between two writes.
classes.ask: Is the second action refused, merged or applied once, and does the record stay consistent?

classes.try: A timeout then a retry of the same write; a retry after a success the client never saw.
classes.ask: Is a retried write applied exactly once, by an idempotency key or a natural key?

classes.try: A dependency that fails halfway through a multi-step write; a batch with one bad item.
classes.ask: Is the whole write rolled back, or the partial result reported item by item?

classes.try: A read-only role, an expired session, a revoked key, a key for another team's surface, no key.
classes.ask: Is every action refused with the right status and no data from anyone else?

value.how_generated: Text, numbers, dates, lists and request bodies come from the seeded generator; races, retries, partial failure and permissions are procedures the plan writes out step by step.

value.title: Interface edges: states to put a page in and what breaks there
value.category_reason: A catalog of interface states, each with what to look for.

states.label: interface.width-320
states.look_for: Sideways page scrolling, cut-off controls, overlapping text.

states.label: interface.zoom-200
states.set_up: Browser zoom at 200 percent on a 1280 pixel window.
states.look_for: Text cut off, controls pushed out of reach, fixed headers or footers covering content.

states.label: interface.long-words
states.set_up: Labels and fields filled with the generator's long word and long token cases.
states.look_for: Boxes that overflow, ellipses that hide meaning, a broken grid.

states.label: interface.right-to-left
states.set_up: The page's right-to-left locale, or dir set to rtl, with right-to-left names filled in.
states.look_for: Layout mirrored wrongly, arrows pointing the wrong way, numbers out of order inside right-to-left text.

states.label: interface.dark-mode
states.look_for: Invisible text, images with transparent backgrounds, contrast that passes only in light.

states.label: interface.reduced-motion
states.look_for: Animations that still run, content that appears only after an animation.

states.label: interface.slow-network
states.set_up: The connection throttled to a slow mobile profile.
states.look_for: No progress shown, a button that can be pressed twice, a timeout with no message.

states.label: interface.offline
states.set_up: The network cut after the page loads.
states.look_for: Typed input lost, silent failures, no way to retry.

states.label: interface.no-javascript
states.look_for: A blank page, a form that cannot submit, content that only scripts draw.

rules: A state with owned_by is that pack's check; run it here only when the plan pairs it with another edge, such as long words at 320 pixels.

Combine two states only when the plan names the pair, such as right-to-left at 320 pixels.
A state the browser cannot be put in is not_run with the reason, never a pass.
Page loads of the local build only: no form is submitted and no account is created to reach a state.

value.title: Video edges: the frames, seconds and players where a cut breaks
value.category_reason: A catalog of video edges, each with its check.

edges.label: video.first-frame
edges.check: Frame 0 is not black or a flash unless declared, and any title on it reads.

edges.label: video.last-frame
edges.check: The last frame holds the end card long enough to read and is not black unless declared.

edges.label: video.captions-at-cuts
edges.check: No caption starts or ends within two frames of a cut without snapping to it, and none hangs across a cut into a new scene.

edges.label: video.silent-edges
edges.check: Silence at the head and tail is under half a second unless declared, and no word is cut off at the end.

edges.label: video.muted
edges.check: Played muted, as autoplay does, the point is clear from the picture and any burned-in text.

edges.label: video.captions-off
edges.check: With captions off, nothing a viewer needs was only in the captions.

edges.label: video.small-screen
edges.check: In a phone player 360 pixels wide, every label and number passes the legibility proxy.

edges.label: video.aspect-ratios
edges.check: Letterboxed or pillarboxed in 16:9, 9:16, 1:1 and 4:5 players, text stays inside the safe area.

edges.label: video.seek
edges.check: Seeking to every cut and to the last second shows the right frame quickly and keeps captions in step.

edges.label: video.loop
edges.check: In a looping player the seam from last frame to first has no audio pop or flash, and the first caption does not show during the last second.

edges.label: video.poster

value.title: API edges: requests a careful service refuses, repeats or rate-limits
value.category_reason: A catalog of API edges, each with the response a careful service gives.

edges.label: api.malformed-json
edges.try: The generator's syntax bodies: truncated, trailing comma, single quotes, comments, NaN, a byte order mark, empty.
edges.expect: 400 with a message; never a 500 and nothing stored.

edges.label: api.content-type
edges.try: The generator's header bodies: text/plain, form encoded, missing, a non-UTF-8 charset.
edges.expect: 415, or a stated rule that is the same every time.

edges.label: api.huge-payload
edges.try: A body one byte past the limit and nesting deeper than any real request.
edges.expect: 413 or 400 before parsing, with memory staying bounded.

edges.label: api.unknown-fields
edges.try: A field the schema does not define.
edges.expect: Refused or ignored by the API's stated rule, every time.

edges.label: api.duplicates-and-big-numbers
edges.try: The same key twice; an integer a double cannot hold exactly; an escape for half a UTF-16 pair.
edges.expect: Refused; never one value silently winning or a number changed.

edges.label: api.idempotency-replay
edges.try: The same write repeated with the same idempotency key and body, then with the same key and a different body, then twice at once.
edges.expect: The first result returned again for the same body, 422 for a different body, 409 while the first is still running, and exactly one write.

edges.label: api.expired-lease
edges.try: A submit after the lease expired, a heartbeat after expiry, and a submit with a stale fencing token after another worker claimed the task.
edges.expect: Refused with a clear status, and the other worker's claim untouched.

edges.label: api.auth
edges.try: No key, an expired session, a revoked key, a key for another team's surface.
edges.expect: 401 or 403 with no data; never a 500.

edges.label: api.method-and-path
edges.try: An unsupported method, a trailing slash, an encoded slash, a very long path.

edges.label: api.rate-limit
edges.try: A burst over the documented limit, against the local build only.
edges.expect: 429 with Retry-After, and service restored after the wait.

rules: Run against a local build with synthetic data; a deployed service is never the target of malformed, huge, replayed or bursty requests.
Read back after every write case: a refused request that still stored something is a failure.
Record the status, the relevant headers and what was stored; never a credential or a token's value.

value.title: Expected results and how a verdict follows from them
value.category_reason: A zero-call rule: the same expectation and observation always give the same verdict.

outcomes.accept_unchanged: Accepted and stored exactly as given.
outcomes.accept_normalized: Accepted in a stated normal form, such as NFC text or trimmed spaces; the plan names the form.
outcomes.reject_with_message: Refused before anything is stored, with a message that names the field and the limit or rule.
outcomes.refuse_status: An API refuses with the stated status code, such as 400, 413, 415, 422 or 429.
outcomes.works_in_state: In the interface state, every function and piece of content the page has still works and shows.
outcomes.meets_check: A video edge passes its check from the video catalog.
outcomes.not_applicable: The class cannot reach this target, with the reason; it is listed, never counted as passing.

always_fail: a hang past the plan's time limit
a value changed in meaning, such as a number off by one or text reordered
half a write stored after a refusal
value.verdict: pass when what was observed is the expected outcome in every detail the plan states; fail otherwise. A case that did not run is listed under not run with its reason.

value.name: edge case generator
value.runtime: Python 3.10 or later, standard library only; nothing to install.
commands: python -m edge_cases generate --kind strings --kind dates --seed 20261030 [--max-length N] [--summary]
does: Labelled cases for text, numbers, dates, lists and JSON request bodies, each with its value, context, an escaped form, sizes and a SHA-256.
The same cases for the same seed and limits on every Python version and platform, from a pinned SplitMix64 stream per kind.
Daylight saving cases from the current rules for New York, London and Lord Howe Island, checked against the time zone database in the tests.

Write any file; the command line prints ASCII-only JSON.
Decide a verdict: the plan's expectations and the run's observations do that.
value.tests: The code's tests check every label's claim with the standard library's Unicode data, datetime and the time zone database, check determinism across processes and hash seeds, and recompute this pack's case set and labels from source.json, in the library's CI job for the pack.

value.title: Generator labels for strings: what each case tests and what a careful target does
value.category_reason: The generator's labelled test inputs for one kind, kept equal to the code by its tests.

strings.empty.expect: Reject when required, with a message naming the field; never store it as a value.

strings.whitespace.space.why: One space looks empty but is not.
strings.whitespace.space.expect: Treat as empty after trimming, or reject.

strings.whitespace.only.expect: Treat as empty after trimming, or reject.

strings.whitespace.no-break-space.why: A no-break space survives most trim functions.
strings.whitespace.no-break-space.expect: Trim Unicode spaces too, or reject.

strings.whitespace.padded.why: Leading and trailing spaces around a real value.
strings.whitespace.padded.expect: Trim once, keep the inner text, and say so if the stored value differs.

strings.size.one-char.expect: Accept unless a minimum says otherwise.

strings.size.at-max.expect: Accept and store all of it.

strings.size.over-max.expect: Reject with the limit in the message; never cut it silently.

strings.size.huge.expect: Reject early, before it is parsed, logged or stored.

strings.size.long-word.why: A long word with no space to break at.
strings.size.long-word.expect: Wrap or scroll inside its box; never overflow the page.

strings.size.long-token.why: A long address-like token with no spaces.
strings.size.long-token.expect: Wrap or scroll inside its box; never overflow the page.

strings.unicode.combining-mark.why: A letter plus a separate accent mark (decomposed form).
strings.unicode.combining-mark.expect: Compare and search after normalizing; never drop the mark.

strings.unicode.precomposed.why: The same name with a single accented letter (composed form).
strings.unicode.precomposed.expect: Equal to the decomposed form after normalizing.

strings.unicode.stacked-marks.why: One letter carrying eight combining marks.
strings.unicode.stacked-marks.expect: Count it as one character on screen and keep the marks inside the line box.

strings.unicode.rtl-arabic.expect: Shown right to left, aligned to the start of its box.

strings.unicode.rtl-hebrew.expect: Shown right to left, aligned to the start of its box.

strings.unicode.rtl-with-digits.why: Right-to-left text mixed with digits and Latin letters.
strings.unicode.rtl-with-digits.expect: Digits and Latin runs keep their order inside the right-to-left text.

strings.unicode.bidi-override.why: A right-to-left override that makes text display in a different order than stored.
strings.unicode.bidi-override.expect: Reject or strip direction controls in names and identifiers, or show them escaped.

strings.unicode.emoji.why: One emoji outside the Basic Multilingual Plane: two UTF-16 units, four UTF-8 bytes.
strings.unicode.emoji.expect: Count it as one character; never split it in half.

strings.unicode.emoji-zwj-family.why: Several emoji joined by zero-width joiners into one picture.
strings.unicode.emoji-zwj-family.expect: Count, cut and delete it as one character on screen.

strings.unicode.emoji-skin-tone.why: An emoji with a skin tone modifier.
strings.unicode.emoji-skin-tone.expect: Keep the modifier attached; never separate the pair.

strings.unicode.flag.why: A flag made of two regional indicator letters.
strings.unicode.flag.expect: Keep the pair together; one half alone shows as a letter box.

strings.unicode.keycap.why: A digit, a variation selector and a combining keycap.

strings.unicode.confusable.why: A Cyrillic letter that looks like a Latin one.
strings.unicode.confusable.expect: Two names that look the same must not both pass as different accounts or labels.

strings.unicode.fullwidth.expect: Normalize for comparison, or reject where only ASCII is allowed.

strings.unicode.ligature.why: A ligature character that compatibility normalization splits into two letters.
strings.unicode.ligature.expect: Search and compare after compatibility normalization where the field is a name or keyword.

strings.unicode.sharp-s.why: Sharp s: upper case is two letters long.
strings.unicode.sharp-s.expect: Case-insensitive compare uses case folding, not upper or lower case.

strings.unicode.dotted-capital-i.why: Capital I with dot: lower case adds a combining mark.
strings.unicode.dotted-capital-i.expect: Case-insensitive compare uses case folding and the length may change.

strings.unicode.non-bmp-ideograph.why: A CJK ideograph outside the Basic Multilingual Plane.
strings.unicode.non-bmp-ideograph.expect: Stored, counted and shown as one character.

strings.zero-width.space.why: An invisible zero-width space inside a word.
strings.zero-width.space.expect: Visible in review, stripped or rejected in identifiers.

strings.zero-width.joiner.why: An invisible zero-width joiner inside a word.
strings.zero-width.joiner.expect: Visible in review, stripped or rejected in identifiers.

strings.zero-width.non-joiner.why: An invisible zero-width non-joiner inside a word.
strings.zero-width.non-joiner.expect: Kept in text where a language needs it; visible in review.

strings.zero-width.byte-order-mark.why: A byte order mark at the start of a value.
strings.zero-width.byte-order-mark.expect: Strip it at input; two values that differ only by it are equal.

strings.zero-width.word-joiner.why: An invisible word joiner inside a word.
strings.zero-width.word-joiner.expect: Visible in review, stripped or rejected in identifiers.

strings.control.newline.why: A line break inside a one-line field.
strings.control.newline.expect: Reject in one-line fields, or keep it and show it as a break; never split a record on it.

strings.control.crlf.why: A carriage return and line feed inside a value.
strings.control.crlf.expect: Never let it start a new header, log line or CSV row.

strings.control.tab.expect: Never let it shift a column in exports.

strings.control.nul.why: A NUL character, which ends strings in C and some databases.
strings.control.nul.expect: Reject, or store and return it unchanged; never truncate at it.

strings.control.line-separator.why: The Unicode line separator, which ends lines in some JavaScript and JSON tools.
strings.control.line-separator.expect: Escape it in scripts and JSON; never break a line on it silently.

strings.markup.angle-brackets.why: Text with angle brackets and an ampersand.
strings.markup.angle-brackets.expect: Shown as text, escaped exactly once, never interpreted as markup.

strings.markup.quotes.why: Single and double quotes in a name.
strings.markup.quotes.expect: Stored and shown unchanged; never closes a quoted string.

strings.markup.template-braces.why: Placeholders that template engines would fill.
strings.markup.template-braces.expect: Shown literally; never filled from other data.

strings.markup.spreadsheet-formula.why: A value a spreadsheet would run as a formula.
strings.markup.spreadsheet-formula.expect: Exports quote or prefix it so a spreadsheet shows it as text.

strings.markup.path-like.why: A value that looks like a path that climbs out of a folder.
strings.markup.path-like.expect: Never used as a path without resolving and confining it.

strings.seeded.mixed.why: Seeded random text mixing letters, digits, marks, right-to-left letters, emoji and invisible characters.
strings.seeded.mixed.expect: Round-trips unchanged; the same seed gives the same text.

value.title: Generator labels for numbers: what each case tests and what a careful target does
value.category_reason: The generator's labelled test inputs for one kind, kept equal to the code by its tests.

numbers.boundary.below-minimum.why: One below the smallest allowed value.
numbers.boundary.below-minimum.expect: Reject with the limit in the message.

numbers.boundary.above-maximum.why: One above the largest allowed value.
numbers.boundary.above-maximum.expect: Reject with the limit in the message.

numbers.boundary.zero.expect: Accept or reject by the field's rule; never treat it as missing.

numbers.sign.negative-one.expect: Reject where counts cannot be negative; never read it as no limit.

numbers.sign.leading-plus.expect: Accept as the same number, or reject with a message.

numbers.integer.max-safe.why: 2**53 - 1, the largest safe integer: it and the integer after it are both exact in an IEEE-754 double.

numbers.integer.max-safe-plus-one.why: 2**53, still exact, but the next integer is not, so a double cannot tell 2**53 from 2**53 + 1.
numbers.integer.max-safe-plus-one.expect: Round-trips exactly or is rejected; never silently changed.

numbers.integer.max-safe-plus-two.expect: Kept exactly, as a string or a big integer, or rejected; never changed by one.

numbers.integer.int32-max.expect: Accept where the field allows it.

numbers.integer.int32-overflow.why: One past the largest signed 32-bit integer.
numbers.integer.int32-overflow.expect: Reject or store in a wider type; never wrap to a negative number.

numbers.integer.int64-max.expect: Accept where the field allows it.

numbers.integer.int64-overflow.why: One past the largest signed 64-bit integer.
numbers.integer.int64-overflow.expect: Reject; never wrap or saturate silently.

numbers.float.one-tenth.why: 0.1, which binary floating point cannot hold exactly.
numbers.float.one-tenth.expect: Money and counts use decimal or integer units, never binary floats.

numbers.float.smallest-subnormal.expect: Not read as zero where zero means something else.

numbers.float.largest.expect: Accept or reject by range; never overflow to infinity.

numbers.float.overflow.why: A literal too large for a double.
numbers.float.overflow.expect: Reject; many parsers turn it into infinity.

numbers.float.many-digits.why: More digits than a double keeps.
numbers.float.many-digits.expect: Round once, by a stated rule, or reject.

numbers.word.nan.why: The word NaN, which some parsers accept as a number.
numbers.word.nan.expect: Reject; it is not equal to itself and breaks sorting and totals.

numbers.format.thousands-comma.why: A thousands comma and a decimal point.
numbers.format.thousands-comma.expect: Parse with the person's locale and show the value back, or reject.

numbers.format.decimal-comma.why: A thousands point and a decimal comma, the reverse of the case above.
numbers.format.decimal-comma.expect: Parse with the person's locale and show the value back, or reject.
